clue.text: Insensitive towards Australian native

parts.note: numb means without feeling, insensitive
at can mean towards, as in 'throw it at me'

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of being unkind to an Indigenous Australian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Australian native' reads as a person, but it is an animal native to Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: The numbat is a small striped termite-eating marsupial found only in Western Australia.

clue.text: An intellect too unfair — what is fair?

parts.note: not just means unfair
a fair ..., one that is pretty, is a beautiful countenance

explanation.surface: A clever person complains about unfairness and asks what fairness really is.
explanation.walkthrough: Someone who is clever as well as attractive is said to be more than merely good-looking; 'fair' plays on fairness and beauty.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom praises a person with brains as well as looks, an intellect as well as beauty.

clue.text: Machine for cutting a dead bird, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be spoken and heard

parts.note: the moa is an extinct flightless New Zealand bird

explanation.surface: A machine kills a bird while cutting grass.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent MOA and MOWER are pronounced alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A mower is a machine for cutting grass or crops.

clue.text: See 1
Hitler's first target was not prepared to retreat

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the whole phrase is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
raw means unprepared or uncooked

explanation.surface: A general describes Hitler's opening campaign and how an army refused to fall back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to retreat' turns WAS RAW back to front as one run of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Germany's invasion of Poland in 1939 aimed first at its capital city, the start of the Second World War.

clue.text: What the inquiring mind seeks to find in Americans — werewolves!

definitions.text: What the inquiring mind seeks to find

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the following words

explanation.surface: Curious people go looking among Americans and discover werewolves.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across AmericANS WERewolves.
explanation.definitionFit: An enquiring mind is looking for the solution or reply to its question.

clue.text: Ipswich Town three men short, perhaps, said to choke

indicators.note: said signals that the words are spoken and heard

parts.words: Ipswich Town three men short, perhaps
parts.note: Ipswich is in Suffolk, and a football team of eleven three short is eight: Suffolk eight

explanation.surface: A football club playing with only eight men might well choke.
explanation.walkthrough: Ipswich Town is a football club in the English county of Suffolk; football teams have eleven players. Spoken, 'Suffolk eight' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To suffocate is to choke or be deprived of air.

clue.text: Bit of a nag becomes wrinkly

definitions.meaning: a nag is a horse, and the ridge between its shoulder blades is a part of it
to shrivel or dry up and wrinkle

explanation.definitionFit: The withers are the highest part of a horse's back; withers is also the verb meaning shrivels.

clue.text: As work plan is flexible, completion of plan maintained?

definitions.text: As work plan is flexible, completion of plan maintained?

indicators.note: maintained means held within, so the anagram keeps the other letter inside it
flexible means bendable, so these letters are bent into a new order
the completion of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A manager notes that a flexible schedule still gets the job finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flexible' rearranges AS WORK PLAN IS, and 'maintained' keeps N (the last letter of 'plan') inside. The adage says work expands to fill the time available for its completion.
explanation.definitionFit: The humorous principle holds that work expands so as to fill the time available for its completion, the joke of a flexible schedule.

clue.text: Wave drowns tug and a voyager secreted within?

indicators.note: to drown something is to submerge it, so one piece covers the others completely

parts.note: to sway is to wave to and fro
to tow is to tug along

explanation.surface: A big sea swamps a tugboat while somebody hides aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic hint: someone hidden inside a ship who travels without paying. 'drowns' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A stowaway is a passenger concealed on a ship or plane to travel without a ticket.

clue.text: As today ref furious, caution on the way

indicators.note: furious suggests wild disorder, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A football match official is angry about something and urges care on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'furious' rearranges the ten letters of AS TODAY REF.
explanation.definitionFit: Being careful on the roads, or caution while travelling, is the notion of safety for road users.

clue.text: American child finds gran not entirely getting into the groove

indicators.note: one piece getting into another means it goes inside it

parts.note: a rut is a groove, such as a wheel track

indicators.note: not entirely means the word is cut short by its last letter

explanation.surface: A child discovers that grandmother is only partly enjoying the music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'groove' sounds musical alongside the gran, but here it is a track or furrow; 'not entirely' drops the final letter and 'getting into' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugrat is American slang for a small child, one who crawls about on the rug.

clue.text: Swoon as knight extracted from passionate paramour

indicators.note: extracted from means taken out of the following words

parts.note: keen can mean passionate or eager
N is the chess abbreviation for a knight
a paramour is a lover

explanation.surface: Someone faints after a knight is pulled away from an ardent suitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extracted from' removes N from KEEN LOVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To keel over is to collapse or faint, which is what swooning does.

clue.text: See 18
Drinks raise heads? No!

parts.note: to cock is to raise or tilt upward, as of an ear
if a coin is not heads it is the other side

explanation.surface: People lift their heads with drinks in hand and someone shouts no.
explanation.walkthrough: A coin toss has two outcomes, so 'heads? No!' points to the other one.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocktails are mixed alcoholic drinks.

clue.text: Singer of many scales?

definitions.meaning: a singer with the lowest male voice
a fish, covered in many scales

explanation.definitionFit: Bass is both the lowest male singing voice and a scaly sea fish.

clue.text: See 1 down
Dance capturing English couple's emotion

indicators.note: capturing means taking in and holding, so the dance surrounds the other piece

parts.note: a fling is a lively Scottish dance, as in Highland fling
E is English and a couple gives two of them

explanation.surface: A dance in which an English pair shows emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: A Highland fling is a Scottish dance; 'capturing' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A feeling is an emotion or sentiment.

clue.text: Duck and dive as a pugilist?

definitions.meaning: to duck and dive is to dodge cleverly and use one's wits
a pugilist is a boxer, so this is boxing in a clever way

explanation.definitionFit: To box clever is a British idiom for acting shrewdly, and literally it is to fight skilfully in the ring.

clue.text: As will flies on flypaper?

parts.note: flies landing on gluey paper get stuck and die, a gummy kind of bad ending

explanation.definitionFit: To come to a sticky end is an idiom for meeting an unpleasant end, here literal for glued flies.

clue.text: Nice sea in district of southeast England, not wide, but green

indicators.note: in places the sea piece inside the trimmed district
not means the next piece is left out

parts.note: the Weald is an area of Kent and Sussex in south-east England
W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide
mer is French for sea, and Nice is in France

explanation.surface: A Riviera sea set in an English region turns out to be green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like the adjective but is the French city, so the sea is in French. 'not' drops the W, leaving EALD, and 'in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Emerald is a bright green colour, named after the gemstone.

clue.text: A crawler on the motorway?

parts.note: a crawler is both a slow vehicle and an insect; a classic small car named after an insect is also a vehicle on the road

explanation.definitionFit: The beetle is a crawling insect and the Volkswagen Beetle is a car seen on motorways.

clue.text: Energy needed with priests worn down

indicators.note: something worn is carried around the body, so the priests wrap round the other piece

parts.note: Catholic priests are addressed as Father
E is the physics abbreviation for energy

explanation.surface: A tired clergy needs vigour after being exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worn' has FATHERS wear E inside them. 'worn down' looks like a phrase for tired, but 'down' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Down is the soft fluffy covering of young birds, a type of fine plumage.

clue.text: Untidy hair — dear, dear

parts.note: a mop is a thick untidy mass of hair
pet is an affectionate name, like dear

explanation.surface: Someone sighs over messy hair, saying 'dear, dear'.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'dear' looks like an exclamation of dismay; the first gives PET and the second is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Moppet is an affectionate term for a small child or darling, used like a pet name.

clue.text: Something in two dimensions which travels in three?

definitions.meaning: an aircraft moves through three-dimensional space

explanation.definitionFit: A plane is a flat surface in geometry and also short for aeroplane.

clue.text: Serving little cakes, returning to consume unspecified number

parts.note: mini means little

indicators.note: to consume is to take in, so the reversed cakes take in the other piece
returning means the word for cakes is read backwards

parts.note: tarts are small pastries or cakes
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: A waiter serves small cakes, coming back to eat an uncertain quantity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns TARTS into STRAT, and 'to consume' puts N inside it to give STRANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Ministrant is a formal adjective meaning attending or serving, as an altar server does.

clue.text: See 9
Smoke fumes for each …

parts.note: gas can mean fumes
per means for each

explanation.surface: A complaint about the fumes given off by each cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: GASPER is old British slang for a cheap cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasper is a slang name for a cigarette, the thing one smokes.

clue.text: … the last of which brings material into fashion

indicators.note: one piece put into another goes inside it

parts.note: a fad is a passing fashion
gen is British slang for information or material

explanation.surface: Continuing the smoke, its final part brings cloth into style.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the previous clue: 'which' is the smoke, so its last bit is the cigarette stub; 'into' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A fag end is the stub of a cigarette ('fag' being British slang), the last remaining part of a smoke.
